CSP and Referrer-Policy are not judged because a fitting value differs per application. A header set only for other paths is not seen. Nothing outside this host is contacted, and neither the body nor cookie values are stored.","recommendation":"No action needed.","settingsURL":null,"isApplicable":false,"isInconclusive":false,"fixAction":null,"cisControl":null,"nistCsf":["PR.PS-01"]},{"category":"Network & Boundary","title":"SPF, DMARC, MTA-STS and Expiry of Your Own Domains","checkId":"server_domain_check","isPassed":true,"statusText":"Not configured (optional check, not applicable)","detail":"An optional check. It runs only when the setting `domain_check_domains` names your own domains (in the form example.com, up to 5). For each one it checks that SPF and DMARC exist, that SPF does not allow everyone to send, and that the registration has 30 days or more left. For a domain with MX records it also checks MTA-STS (the _mta-sts TXT record and the policy file): not using MTA-STS is only noted, but announcing it while the policy file cannot be fetched, is malformed or does not list every real MX host fails the check. CAA and DNSSEC are shown for information and never fail the check. Only with this setting does anything leave the host, and only three things: (1) dig asks the resolver in /etc/resolv.conf for the TXT, CAA, DS and MX records of the domain (and the _mta-sts TXT record for a domain with MX records); (2) curl reads IANA's public list (which holds no domain name) to find the registry of the TLD, then sends the domain name to that registry's RDAP server to read the expiry date; (3) only for a domain that has MX records and an _mta-sts TXT record, curl reads the policy file from the domain's own host (https://mta-sts.(domain)/.well-known/mta-sts.txt), with certificate checks on and redirects not followed. The result is remembered for six hours.","recommendation":"To check your own domains, set them, for example `sudo roamswitch server config set domain_check_domains example.com` (comma-separated, up to 5). Without the setting nothing is sent.","settingsURL":null,"isApplicable":false,"isInconclusive":false,"fixAction":null,"cisControl":null,"nistCsf":["PR.PS-01"]},{"category":"Network & Boundary","title":"LLMNR / NBNS / mDNS responders","checkId":"server_name_resolution_exposure","isPassed":true,"statusText":"No LLMNR, NBNS or mDNS responder","detail":"When a name is not found in DNS, a host that also asks the whole local network (LLMNR, NBNS) can be answered by any other device there, which then receives the connection (LLMNR / NBT-NS poisoning).
